The Chief Executive’s Report is presented to elected members at each SDCC monthly 
meeting. It forms a key part of our governance and oversight framework, supporting members 
in their role by providing timely updates on the work of the Council.
In line with Section 136(2) of the Local Government Act 2001 (as amended by the Local 
Government Reform Act 2014), the report outlines the performance of executive functions, 
the implementation of Council policy, and the delivery of services across the organisation.
This report should be read alongside updates provided to Area Committee Meetings and the 
quarterly Capital Progress Report, which together offer a comprehensive view of Council 
activity and progress.
Each edition includes:
•	Updates on how we are delivering on our Corporate Plan goals
•	Highlights of major initiatives and events
•	A visual snapshot of recent community and Council activities
The report also provides an opportunity to shine a light on areas of our work that may not 
always be in the spotlight but are vital to the day-to-day life of the county.

Climate Leadership
Dublin local authorities’ fashion film launches in style
“Losing the Thread: The Cost of Fast 
Fashion”, a collaboration between the 
four Dublin local authorities, premiered 
on Friday, 3 October at the Lighthouse 
Cinema in Smithfield. The film, which 
was produced with funding from the 
Department of Climate, Energy and 
the Environment, takes an honest look 
at Ireland’s fast fashion problem by 
exploring environmental impacts and 
ethical dilemmas as well as sharing the 
views of shoppers on Dublin’s streets.  It 
concludes with practical and inspiring 
steps to address the issues raised, 
featuring expert opinions from Ireland’s 
growing circular economy sector.
Community Action Tackles Illegal Dumping
Following a successful application 
to Dublin City Council as the waste 
enforcement regional lead authority, 
three community anti-dumping initiatives 
were implemented in South Dublin over 
recent months with the €61k grant 
funding received.
Firstly, a two-week radio campaign 
highlighted producers’ responsibilities for 
litter and waste disposal.  This involved 
a series of adverts which reached over 
284,000 listeners on local radio stations 
Q102 and FM104 and it also saw a 
further 50,000 digital ads being sent to 
smart devices.
A second scheme addressed repeated 
dumping at a specific location in West 
Tallaght.  In this instance, funding 
supported the installation of extra 
public lighting, to help deter dumping of 
household waste adjacent to a new multi-
use games area along with CCTV also 
directed at the site.  This intervention has 
proved effective, with no further incidents 
of illegal dumping reported to date.
The third scheme was a mattress amnesty 
in the run up to Halloween which saw 
eight dedicated drop-off events take 
place in the community, along with 
the opportunity to bring unwanted 
mattresses to our project partners site 
in Clondalkin.  1,225 matresses were 
diverted from landfill and recycled by 
our project partners in Bounce Back 
Recylcing based in Clondalkin.  Bounce 
Back are a social enterprise who deliver 
social, environmental & societal impacts 
that make economic sense, and they 
collaborated with our environmental 
awareness team to make the amnesty 
days become community recycling days 
offering free WEEE collections while our 
staff were on hand to share advice on 
environmental issues.
The launch event which was attended by 
over 150 students from across Dublin 
combined education and inspiration, 
and included a circular clothes swap, 
upcycling workshops, expert advice 
and an interactive panel discussion 
with circular economy specialists.  Over 
two hundred items of clothing were 
exchanged at the fully circular swap shop.
Both the film and the launch reflect the 
commitment of the four Dublin local 
authorities to supporting the circular 
economy and reducing textile waste and 
the film is now available to view on www.
mywaste.ie which is Ireland’s official guide 
to managing waste.

Climate Leadership
Sustainable Development Goals events a success
A variety of events took place during SDG 
Week, held from 20 to 27 September this 
year. 
Activities included an energy and 
sustainable living workshop for Women’s 
Collective Lucan, educational walks in 
Corkagh and Tymon parks led by our park 
rangers, and a Lunch & Learn session in 
county hall. The Lunch & Learn focused 
on the Sustainable Development Goals, 
highlighting actions being taken and 
inspiring practical ideas for everyday life.
Participants discovered how small 
changes can help achieve the Global 
Goals, from simple ways to protect the 
planet to ideas for saving money and 
living more sustainably. The interactive 
quiz and hands-on workshop encouraged 
everyone to test their knowledge and 
try new approaches. Many enjoyed the 
chance to win sustainable prizes, which 
added a fun and competitive element to 
the experience.
The week provided an ideal opportunity 
to meet others and build connections. 
Positive feedback and strong attendance 
reflected a shared commitment to 
sustainability, both at work and at home.
Thank you to all who facilitated, attended 
and contributed to making these events 
successful. There is great anticipation for 
future opportunities to learn, connect and 
work together towards a more sustainable 
future.
Progressing Active Travel in South Dublin
Our Active South Dublin plan delivering 
active travel and sustainable transport 
options continues to support climate 
action and healthier lifestyles in 
neighbourhoods across the county. 
Several major projects, as outline dbelow 
have made significant progress this year 
making it safer and easier for everyone 
to walk, cycle and move around their 
communities.
D24 Neighbourhood Cycle Network
The second phase of the D24 network 
began in May 2024 with the construction 
of a new junction at Ballycullen Drive and 
Ballycullen Road delivering protected 
cycle lanes as well as pedestrian 
crossings on the three arms of the 
junction.   Construction of five kilometres 
of segregated cycle lanes using 
reallocated road space followed this.  12 
new pedestrian crossing facilities were 
constructed, four of which are directly 
linked to school access, while the levels 
of two existing pedestrian crossings on 
Killininny Road were raised making them 
more prominent and visible to road users.
The project also saw footpath widening 
and relocation of public lighting columns 
on approximately 200 metres of path 
in front of two primary schools on 
Ballycullen Drive.  Lighting was also 
added to a permeability route from 
Killininny Road to the community centre, 
football club and men’s shed and school 
zone works including rondels and pencil 
bollards were carried out at three schools.
Construction works on this phase were 
completed last month at a total cost

of €5.2 million including VAT with 
works funded by the National Transport 
Authority.  Initial traffic speed data in 
the area following the works shows a 
reduction of a 7-day average speed from 
55 km/h to 40 km/h at the location of a 
new raised table pedestrian crossing on 
Killininny Road which provide access to 
two primary schools.
Construction of the nearby Firhouse 
Road scheme next year will see this this 
infrastructure connect directly to the 
Dodder Greenway enhancing regional 
active travel connectivity.
Castletymon Road Active Travel Scheme 
Phase 1.2 of the Castletymon Road 
active travel scheme, running from the 
Tymon Park entrance to Greenhills Road, 
is close to completion. This section 
will link to the completed Castletymon 
district enhancement and the earlier 
phase of works, further expanding the 
local cycle track network providing safer 
and sustainable travel options for local 
people.
The initial phase, measuring 1.2 
kilometres, introduces new cycle tracks 
and improved crossings for pedestrians 
and cyclists at key junctions, connecting a 
district centre, three schools and several 
residential estates.  The final phase, 
which will extend from Castletymon 
Road Library to Main Street, is expected 
to begin construction in 2026. Once 
finished, the Castletymon Road active 
Climate Leadership
travel scheme will connect to the Dodder 
Greenway and the future Greenhills 
BusConnects scheme, significantly 
expanding the cycle network across 
Tallaght and the wider area.
This project is part of a national 
Pathfinder Programme, a collection of 
thirty-five transport initiatives designed 
to be exemplary and innovative, with the 
scheme trialling a new cycle-friendly kerb 
that is now serving as a model for similar 
projects across Ireland.
Grand Canal to Lucan Urban Greenway
Construction of phase one of the Grand 
Canal to Lucan Urban Greenway (Canal 
Loop) began in March this year and is 
expected to finish by the end of this 
year.  By October, 80% of pathways were 
complete and approximately half of the 
park entrances are finished.
When complete, the scheme will provide 
2.2 kilometres of new greenway and 
nearly one kilometre of links and spurs 
that provide connections to four schools 
as well as Lucan Sports & Leisure 
Centre, Griffeen Valley Park and local 
neighbourhoods.
The project also includes new public 
lighting, improved crossings and 
upgraded park entrances, all of which 
are designed to make movement easier 
for pedestrians and cyclists in line with 
universal design principles.  In addition, 
more than one hundred new trees will 
be planted throughout the park, along 
with native and wildflower meadows and 
shrubs.
We are committed to progressing the 
next phase of the project, which will link 
the N4 to Lucan Village, and scheduling 
for this will be examined in the context 
of available funding and resources of our 
overall Cycle South Dublin programme.

Quality Housing
Funding Management and Maintenance of our Social Housing Stock
With increased housing delivery over the last 
five years, SDCC currently manages over 
10,500 social homes.  However, this stock 
ranges in age from homes originally built 
in the middle of the 1900s right up to the 
high-quality modern homes added in recent 
years.
Given the profile of our housing stock, 
we are currently undertaking condition 
surveys to fully understand and plan 
for the scale of investment required to 
ensure a common quality standard for our 
social homes.  1,200 surveys have been 
commissioned so far and the initial results 
of these show a significant requirement for 
additional planned maintenance, energy 
efficiency and upgrade works for windows, 
kitchens, bathrooms, electrical and heating 
systems.  As these surveys progress next 
year, we will develop a planned programme 
of investment to deliver these works over 
future years.  The costs of such plans 
will be significant and, together with the 
impact of inflation and increased costs for 
materials, direct labour and contractors, 
coupled with increases to Local Property 
Tax and insurance and various other costs 
that are borne by the council in managing 
our housing stock, will necessitate additional 
funding.  For example, in 2024 our average 
maintenance cost per unit reached €1,733 
per home per annum and average relet 
costs were at €31,286, and that is without 
including many of the other management 
and upgrade costs that are involved in 
looking after a large housing stock.
Rental income has grown significantly in 
recent years, with €35m in income from 
our stock last year, and this is projected to 
continue to increase for 2025 and 2026 but 
is not anticipated to be sufficient to meet 
the level of investment required for response 
and planned maintenance well as all other 
management costs beyond that.  Borrowing 
for such investment would incur significant 
financing costs that would ultimately have 
to be funded from rental income anyway 
so the most sustainable and viable source 
of funding will be through a review of our 
differential rent scheme, particularly in the 
context of the historically low relative rents 
charged by SDCC for some households 
compared to other Dublin local authorities 
and indeed local authorities nationwide.
Independent and thorough analysis and 
comparison of differential rent schemes 
nationwide by the Local Government Audit 
Service is nearing completion and will 
provide a strong evidential basis for strategic 
adjustment of our differential rent scheme 
to address inequities in the current rent 
scheme along with ensuring that sufficient 
funding is in place to meet future social 
housing management and maintenance 
costs.
Each local authority currently has autonomy 
in determining how social housing rents are 
set through a differential rent scheme which 
is a function of the council’s executive, and 
we are very conscious that any adjustments 
to the scheme must first and foremost be 
equitable and affordable for our tenants, 
while also being sufficient to meet all of the 
costs involved in managing, maintaining and 
upgrading our social homes in to the future. 
Accordingly, in 2026 we will present our 
social housing future investment plan to the 
Housing Strategic Committee along with the 
analysis supporting a review and overhaul 
of the current differential rent scheme to 
ensure long-term sustainable funding for 
the plan.

Quality Housing
Meet our Housing Maintenance Team
The SDCC housing maintenance team are 
committed to ensuring that our tenants’ 
homes are safe, secure and well-maintained 
and we want to highlight their role in 
providing repair services to more than 
10,000 properties managed by the council.
Every day, our dedicated team of 45 skilled 
staff who operate from Jobstown Depot 
provide vital services to tenants across 
the county including fixing plumbing 
and carpentry issues or helping to get 
our recently vacant properties back into 
use for households to call home.  The 
team includes a range of roles including 
engineers, clerk of works, foremen, 
plumbers, carpenters, plasters, painters, 
drivers, general operatives, and caretakers, 
delivering a wide range of services through 
direct labour along with managing works 
of specialist contractors who support their 
work.
We are continually working to improve the 
quality of services provided and the team’s 
focus is on ensuring a responsive repair 
service to our tenants for both routine 
maintenance issues and emergencies, 
including out-of-hours work as required.  
The team also manage an extensive 
programme of planned maintenance 
works including energy efficiency 
upgrades, window/door replacement, 
kitchen/bathroom upgrades and external 
refurbishments while partners carry out 
specialist works such as electrical repairs 
and gas boiler servicing which are essential 
to ensure the comfort and safety of 
residents.
Last year the team carried out 12,252 
response repairs to homes at a cost of 
€7.9million while we also delivered €15.5 
million of works on pre-let repairs, planned 
maintenance and energy efficiency works.   
While there are continuing challenges with 
costs of delivering these services due to 
inflation and the costs of labour, materials 
and contractors, we have continued to 
increase our investment in the maintenance 
service with additional staff and funding to 
meet our responsibilities.  
This is accompanied by the ongoing work 
by the team to improve the efficiency and 
technology associated with the service 
while also working to better support 
vulnerable and older tenants, ensuring 
their requests are handled with care and 
urgency, all with the aim of meeting our 
corporate objective of providing quality 
housing in South Dublin.

National Women’s Enterprise Day
A Thriving Economy
National Women’s Enterprise Day (NWED) 
took place on 16 October in Dublin City as 
part of Ireland’s flagship event for women 
in business which is designed to celebrate 
and accelerate female entrepreneurship.
The regional event, officially opened 
by Minister for Enterprise, Tourism 
and Employment Peter Burke TD, was 
organised by the four Dublin Local 
Enterprise Offices. More than three 
hundred women attended on the day, 
with the event hosted by Dublin LEO 
Dublin City. Female founders and business 
leaders from all four local authority areas 
in Dublin were welcomed.
The day was led by Newstalk’s Jess Kelly 
while Ciara Troy, founder of Oishii Foods, 
delivered the keynote address, sharing her 
journey from starting a Dublin market stall 
to building Ireland’s leading handmade 
sushi brand. Helen McNulty, comedian, 
storyteller and businesswoman, also 
offered unique insights with a comedic 
twist. 
Life and leadership coach Alana Kirk 
presented a spotlight session titled 
“What beliefs are holding you back, why 
you have them and how to bust them,” 
aimed at helping women live a better, 
bolder, brighter life. Louise O’Connor from 
Rethink Digital Advisory led a session on 
embracing technology to achieve goals, 
drawing on her twenty years of experience 
in digital transformation.
The event also featured a fireside chat 
and panel discussion with the four Dublin 
#NWED ambassadors: Sylvia Kennedy 
representing LEO Dublin City, Wynne 
Li from LEO Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown, 
Cuty Gupta representing LEO Fingal and 
Dr. Mamobo Ogoro of LEO South Dublin, 
and concluded with a closing address by 
Grainne Denning, Head of Enterprise at 
LEO Dublin City, who emphasised the 
importance of using LEO supports to grow 
businesses.
This was a great opportunity for 
networking and collaboration and 
participants were able to access lots of 
information on supports available from 
a range of agencies at the information 
stands on the day, ensuring lasting impact 
on the local women in business who were 
present.
Women in Business Event at Work IQ 
Meet the Entrepreneur, a women in business 
event, took place in Work IQ, Tallaght on 
16 October as part of LEO South Dublin 
programme for its Network of Enterprising 
Women in South Dublin (NEWS). The key 
objectives of NEWS are to make it easy for 
local female businesswomen to develop 
mutually beneficial relationships with like-
minded entrepreneurs and to support the 
development of women in business in the 
county.
For the event, Sarah Naylor hosted a fireside 
interview with Dr. Mamobo Ogoro, LEO 
South Dublin’s ambassador for National 
Women’s Enterprise Day.  Mamobo is chief 
executive of Gorm Media and based in Rua 
Red Arts Centre in Tallaght.   Dr. Rosalind 
Beere, a serial entrepreneur, lecturer, 
presenter and author specialising in 
strategy and entrepreneurship, also spoke 
at the event.
Both speakers shared their entrepreneurial 
journeys and discussed how they 
consistently work on building their 
brands. They offered advice on engaging 
and following up with new clients. With 
approximately fifty people in attendance, 
the event was very well received and 
included a lively question and answer 
session with strong engagement from the 
audience.

A Thriving Economy
Products from four clients of LEO 
South Dublin are now available in Aldi 
stores nationwide as part of Grow with 
Aldi this year. Garnacha, Happy Hour 
Foods, Niks Tea and Sadie’s Kitchen 
were all finalists in the programme, 
with their products on shelves since 
September.
Grow with Aldi, delivered in partnership 
with Bord Bia, supports Ireland’s 
most ambitious food and drink 
entrepreneurs. This year’s thirty 
finalists represented fifteen counties, 
each product reflecting innovation, 
passion and dedication to quality. After 
a trial period in one hundred sixty-four 
Aldi stores, Aldi will award contracts to 
a select number of winners.
Best wishes to the LEO South Dublin 
clients: Garnacha is a small Irish-
Mexican salsa brand run by Andrea 
from Mexico and Andrew from Ireland. 
Happy Hour Foods supplies Brazilian 
savoury snacks made with high quality 
Irish ingredients, ready in minutes. 
Niks Tea is an award-winning supplier 
of bespoke and speciality teas 
from around the world and Sadie’s 
Kitchen is an innovative food company 
specialising in delicious and nutritious 
bone broth.
Fortivum Consulting Opens Headquarters at Work IQ 
Fortivum Consulting, an Irish engineering 
firm, has officially opened its new 
headquarters at Work IQ in Tallaght, 
creating fifty highly skilled jobs and 
doubling its workforce. 
The company delivers complex datacentre 
and infrastructure projects in seven 
countries and has chosen South Dublin as 
the hub for its international operations.
At the launch event, which was officially 
opened by Minister for Enterprise, Tourism 
and Employment Peter Burke TD, chief 
executive Robert Tobin said, “This isn’t 
just about opening a new office, it’s about 
building something bigger. We’re creating 
opportunities for people to build exciting, 
global careers right here in Ireland.” This 
marks positive news for job creation in 
South Dublin and highlights the growing 
role of Work IQ in supporting the growth 
and development of small and medium 
enterprises in the county.
Fortivum’s expansion includes a planned 
collaboration with Technological University 
Dublin (Tallaght Campus) to establish 
graduate learning pathways for engineers, 
project managers and technical specialists.
This partnership demonstrates the role 
of Work IQ as a catalyst for collaboration 
between enterprise and education, a key 
objective of our economic strategy.
Through Work IQ, we are fostering an 
environment that supports innovation, skills 
development and sustainable economic 
growth, positioning Tallaght and the wider 
county as leaders in Ireland’s knowledge-
driven economy.
LEO South Dublin Clients Growing with Aldi
South Dublin Chamber Awards 2025
More than 360 people attended the 
annual South Dublin Chamber Awards 
at the Maldron Hotel Tallaght on 16 
October. 
The event celebrated the best in 
business and provided local businesses 
with the chance to network, build new 
relationships and enjoy an evening 
that showcased the diverse range of 
successful businesses in the county.
The event was hosted by Marty Whelan 
and the business person of the year 
award went to John Kearns, chief 
executive of Partas. John has driven 
dynamic change in the local economy 
for many years, overseeing the launch 
of Tallaght’s new food market at Priory 
Market and managing enterprise centres 
in Tallaght, Killinarden, Brookfield and 
The Edge – Bolbrook.
Other winners included An Cosán 
as best not-for-profit business, The 
Address CityWest as best place to 
eat, ACE Enterprise Park as best 
small business, Red Mountain as best 
start-up, Fanagans as best family-
owned business and Jay Patel as best 
networker.  
Other local businesses including TEC, 
Arcadia, SCD Leisure, Wilsons Auctions 
and Thorntons Recycling also received 
awards along with Sinead Murphy from 
AIB who received the employee of the 
year award.

Working Together for Safer Roads
A Better Place
East Coast local authorities, including 
SDCC, worked with roads policing on 
a multi-agency Project EDWARD Day—
Every Day Without a Road Death—in 
September. 
Project EDWARD Day is an annual road 
safety awareness initiative, highlighting 
the impact of collisions and aiming 
for one day each year free from road 
fatalities. 
The initiative encourages all road users 
to pause and consider the risks they face, 
the risks they may pose to others, and 
how these risks can be reduced. Since its 
inception, Project EDWARD has grown 
each year, supported by governments, 
emergency services, road safety 
organisations and Irish businesses.
Our road safety officer Orlaith Maguire 
secured permission and support from the 
owners of Project EDWARD, a UK-based 
road safety initiative, to use the name in 
Ireland as part of the multi-agency day. 
The event was successful and marked 
the first time the Irish-based initiative 
achieved its goal—a full day without a 
road fatality.
National Road Safety Week began on 
6 October, when we hosted a road 
safety themed day throughout the week 
and delivering road safety education 
programmes in participating schools. 
The week concluded with National 
Child Safety Day on Friday, 10 October, 
featuring a road safety walk around 
Clondalkin village with students from St 
Joseph’s BNS Clondalkin, supported by 
An Garda Síochána.
2025 Accessibility Improvements
Additional funds totalling €400,000 
were allocated in the council’s 2025 
budget to deliver a range of local 
accessibility improvements, with a 
particular focus on upgrading footpaths 
and installing dishings. In particular, the 
allocation supported an extension of 
the footpath network at Fonthill Road, 
while significant funding went towards 
upgrades at Anne Devlin Drive, Bawnlea 
Estate, Edenbrook Park, Elkwood, Esker 
Lawns, Killinarden Estate, Kilmartin 
Gardens, Lindisfarne Estate, Oakcourt 
Estate (dishings at all crossings), 
Palmers Road, Riversdale Estate, St 
Patricks Cottages, Wheatfield Estate and 
Woodfarm Estate.
These enhancements aim to create 
safer, more inclusive public spaces for all 
residents, especially those with mobility 
needs, and we will continue to address 
any specific issues identified across 
the county so if there are accessibility 
challenges at particular locations 
please let us know by emailing info@
sdublincoco.ie and we will aim to address 
them promptly.
IPI Award Winner - Work IQ Innovation Centre
The Irish Planning Institute’s awards 
ceremony took place at Clontarf Castle, 
Dublin, recognising excellence in 
planning. In 2025, the institute marks 
its fiftieth anniversary, celebrating five 
decades of commitment to sustainable 
development and community-focused 
planning across Ireland.
Outstanding projects were 
acknowledged, including Work IQ 
Innovation Centre, which received the 
award in the commercial project category 
for supporting a prosperous economy 
while integrating climate action and 
sustainable travel.
Nominations were also received for 
urban regeneration, with Connecting 
Communities Through the Regeneration 
of West Tallaght Parks, research and 
innovation for the housing supply monitor, 
and for the planning authority award.
The awards reflected a range of 
significant achievements in the planning 
profession throughout Ireland along with 
the role of planners in inspiring continued 
excellence in creating sustainable and 
vibrant communities.

Magical Christmas Celebrations Across South Dublin! 
Get ready for Christmas in South Dublin! 
There will be markets, music, and festive 
fun for everyone. Christmas Markets start 
on Friday, 28 November in Clondalkin, with 
local crafts, treats, and the lighting of the 
Christmas tree at the Civic Offices. On 
Friday 5 December, Parthalán Place will 
be illuminated as the venue for the South 
Dublin Christmas Markets, a festive day of 
food and craft stalls including the lighting 
of the tree with choral performances from 
local groups. This event aims to further 
establish Parthalán Place as a vibrant year-
round community space.
The celebrations then continue across the 
county at the beautiful Lucan House on 
Sunday 7 December, and at the enchanting 
Rathfarnham Castle Park on Sunday 14 
December. Each market will showcase 
talented local traders, seasonal food and 
drink, and a wonderful festive atmosphere.
Adding even more sparkle to the season, 
the Ice Rink at The Square Shopping 
Centre, Tallaght, proudly supported by 
SDCC, opens on Friday 21 November, 
running right through to early January, 
offering families and friends the perfect 
place to glide into the Christmas mood.
And that’s not all, the Christmas Circus 
also opens on Friday 21 November, at 
Lucan House, bringing laughter, wonder, 
and spectacular performances to delight 
audiences young and old.
So, wrap up warm, gather your loved ones, 
and join us as we celebrate Christmas 
across South Dublin with a season full of 
joy, entertainment, and community spirit.
Connected Communities
The spirit of education and opportunity 
was celebrated as Mayor Pamela Kearns 
joined representatives from TU Dublin, 
South Dublin County Council’s Community 
Department, and proud families for the 
annual Education Bursary Awards Ceremony, 
held on Tuesday, 14 October 2025, at Work 
IQ in the Innovation Quarter, Tallaght.
Under the initiative, 13 TU Dublin students 
received €2,500 towards their 2025–2026 
academic costs: eight first-year and five 
second-year students are continuing their 
studies with the programme’s support. 
Established in 2006 through a partnership 
between South Dublin County Council 
and TU Dublin, the Education Bursary 
Programme supports young people from 
partner DEIS schools in the county who may 
face financial barriers to continuing their 
third-level education.
Mayor Kearns congratulated the students, 
praising their hard work and determination. 
“I am so pleased to celebrate your 
achievements and to see the lasting impact 
this programme has on young people across 
the South Dublin County Council area,” she 
said, offering encouragement to the first-
year students as they begin their academic 
journey, and commending the progress of 
the  second-year students.
The Mayor also thanked TU Dublin for 
the continued partnership with SDCC, 
highlighting the shared commitment to, 
and importance of, education in local 
communities.

Bronntanas – Giving the gift of Irish!
Bronntanas, a new Irish language family 
arts festival, took place from 25 to 
27 September and offered a weekend 
of engaging experiences designed to 
encourage parents and children to speak 
Irish together. 
The festival began as an idea developed 
by our Irish Language Officer Muireann 
Ní Cheannabháin and was celebrated 
across the county through the Gaeilge 
365 network, in partnership with Dublin 
City Council, Fingal County Council and 
Dún Laoghaire Rathdown County Council, 
with support from the Department of 
Rural and Community Development, the 
Gaeltacht, Glór na nGael and COGG.
Over thirty free events attended by 675 
people, Bronntanas brought the Irish 
language to life for all ages and fluency 
levels. With 500 registrations, the 21-
day home challenge Bronntanas Beo is 
designed to help families build new habits 
with Gaeilge sa bhaile. SDCC played 
a central role in shaping the festival’s 
programme, collaborating with artists to 
create unique and interactive experiences 
for families.
Highlights included Biongó na nEachtrán 
with HK Ní Shioradáin, where families 
learned Irish through a fun bingo game 
with friendly aliens, and An Leabharlannaí 
Craiceáilte with Seán T. Ó Meallaigh, an 
interactive library performance full of 
laughter and vibrant language. Mistéir, 
led by Aideen McQueen and Louisa Ní 
Cultural Richness
Éidéain, invited families to solve a live 
mystery using their Irish skills, while 
Cogadh Dearg with Cara Dunne offered 
a colourful team game for children and 
parents.
Every event was designed to create 
lasting memories and foster a love for 
the Irish language in family settings.

Redline Festival 2025
The Red Line Book Festival returned from 
13 to 19 October this year, welcoming 
more than 5,500 attendees of all ages to 
over forty events across twelve venues. 
Curated and designed by the programming 
and events team in SDCC Libraries, the 
festival continues to position the county as 
a vibrant cultural hub, promoting literacy, 
learning, and community engagement.
This year’s programme featured celebrated 
literary figures from Ireland and abroad. 
Acclaimed Bridget Jones creator Helen 
Fielding, Booker award winner Paul Lynch, 
renowned political correspondent Gavan 
Reilly, Irish language advocate Hector in 
conversation with Muireann O’Connell, 
and best-selling author John Connell were 
among the highlights.
Emerging writers were championed 
throughout the festival, with opportunities 
to share their work and connect with 
audiences. One notable event saw Tallaght 
native Luke Devlin discuss his debut novel 
with author Claire Hennessy in North 
Clondalkin Library.
Younger library users took centre stage with 
events designed to encourage creativity 
and fun. Alan Nolan’s new play, Molly 
Malone and Bram Stoker in the Curious 
Case of the Irish Yeti, sold out all four 
shows in the Civic theatre main space. The 
Family Fun Day in Tallaght Library was a full 
day of sold-out activities, while Parthalán 
Place transformed into a colourful 
wonderland with music, games and literary 
characters animating the space.
The Red Line Residency, supported by 
the Arts Office, remains a festival staple. 
Illustrator in Residence Celina Buckley 
worked with fifteen artists over five weeks, 
culminating in a curated exhibition launched 
in Ballyroan Library on the festival’s opening 
night.
Accessibility and inclusion were prioritised 
this year. ISL interpretation was available at 
select events, buses operated from select 
libraries, and sensory spaces and activities 
were offered at various venues. Feedback 
was overwhelmingly positive, with particular 
praise for the inclusion of Irish Sign 
Language.
Local history featured with the launch 
of Tallaght: A Welcoming Space, an oral 
history project curated by Liz Gillis and 
launched by Cllr. Pamela Kearns. The 
project includes contributions from notable 
Tallaght residents, reflecting on their lives 
and the changes in the area over the years.
The continued success of the Red Line 
Book Festival reflects SDCC’s commitment 
to fostering creativity, literacy and cultural 
participation. This year’s festival once again 
demonstrated the power of books and 
storytelling to connect people, spark ideas 
and celebrate creativity throughout the 
county.

Accessibility Week 2025 
SDCC is looking forward to celebrating 
Accessibility Week 2025, running 
3 – 10 December. The week begins 
on International Day of Persons with 
Disabilities and ends on International 
Human Rights Day, signifying the reality of 
disability rights as human rights. 
Accessibility Week raises awareness about 
disability, equality, and inclusion, and 
celebrates wellbeing and accessibility 
across the county. 
We’re planning a lively week of activities, 
including:

A social media campaign
•	
Inclusive sports events
•	
Special activities in libraries
A highlight of the week will be an 
interactive staff workshop with human 
rights expert Niall Crowley, taking place in 
the SDCC Foyer on 10th December. 
The session will look at how the Council 
meets its responsibilities under Public 
Sector Equality and Human Rights Duty, 
which sets out our equality and human 
rights obligations.

Staff Safety and Wellbeing Seminar
As part of our annual Safety and 
Wellbeing Seminar, Staff attended an 
engaging and thought-provoking theatre 
performance of “Distraction” on 21 
October as part of the annual safety and 
wellbeing seminar. The production by 
Theatre at Work highlighted how small 
lapses in concentration while driving 
can have serious consequences. The 
performance introduced the important 
theme of safe driving in an entertaining 
way and sparked conversations long 
after the curtain fell.
Leo Lieghio, vice president of the Irish 
Road Victims’ Association, shared his 
personal story about the human impact 
of road traffic collisions following the 
death of his daughter Marsia twenty 
years ago. 
Leo offered a powerful reminder of 
the need to improve road safety for 
everyone. The Irish Road Victims’ 
Association provides free support 
to victims and families, including 
counselling, legal advice and help 
through investigations and court 
proceedings. This seminar is a key event 
in the staff calendar each year, giving 
both outdoor and indoor staff the 
chance to come together, reflect and 
refresh.

Our Strategy to respond to the Revised Housing Growth Requirements
SDCC has conducted a detailed analysis 
of current zoned land capacity and a 
deliverability assessment for residential 
development in the County to respond to 
the National Planning Framework (NPF) 
Implementation Guidelines for Housing 
Growth Requirements.
The revised NPF sets a target for us 
to deliver approximately 47,000 new 
homes by 2040, with annual targets of 
3,270 units up to 2034 and 2,414 units 
thereafter. The Settlement Capacity Audit 
found that currently zoned land could 
accommodate about 35,480 dwellings 
by 2040, with an additional 21,695 units 
possible on long-term zoned land.
However, the deliverability assessment 
reveals a significant challenge: by 2028, 
we are forecasting a shortfall of 2,086 
homes compared to the baseline target 
of 11,699 units for that period. This gap 
widens to over 10,000 units by 2040 
unless further lands are zoned and 
activated. The assessment highlights that, 
while the current rate of housing delivery 
is strong and on target for previous target, 
the pipeline of available zoned lands is 
insufficient to meet the increased housing 
targets. 
The main constraint is the limited supply 
of immediately developable land, 
especially as some key non-strategic sites 
have already been built out.
To address this, the Chief Executive 
will prepare a proposed variation to the 
Development Plan to zone additional land 
capable of delivering up to c7,900 homes. 
This figure covers both the anticipated 
shortfall and the “additional provision” 
recommended by national guidelines, 
ensuring flexibility and resilience in the 
housing supply pipeline.
Site selection will be guided by robust 
criteria: sites must support compact 
growth, be within or adjacent to the built-
up area, have access to high-capacity 
public transport, be serviceable within 
five years, and offer or enable social 
infrastructure. Sites should be free 
from significant legal, environmental, or 
servicing constraints.
To ensure transparency and public 
engagement, we have commenced a non-
statutory consultation (23rd October – 
13th November) calling for lands to be 
put forward which meet our suitability 
criteria which align with national, regional 
and local planning and environmental 
policy. This evidence-based, criteria-driven 
approach aims to ensure South Dublin can 
sustainably meet its housing needs and 
national policy objectives.
Additionally, we are focused on long-
term planning and the Chief Executive 
recommends earmarking new Strategic 
Development Areas (SDAs) to enable a 
plan led approach to strategic transport-
oriented development, ensuring that the 
Council can respond flexibly to future 
housing needs beyond 2030. 
Through these measures—zoning 
additional residential land, engaging the 
public, and planning for future SDAs—we 
are aiming to ensure that South Dublin 
can sustainably meet its housing needs 
and national policy objectives, balancing 
growth with community and environmental 
priorities.
The Chief Executive’s report, detailing 
these findings and recommendations, was 
formally presented at the October Council 
meeting and has been circulated to both 
the Office of the Planning Regulator 
(OPR) and the Minister for Housing, Local 
Government and Heritage.

New Facilities at Tymon Park
Tymon Park has recently seen the opening 
of new and welcome additions that further 
enhance SDCC’s largest regional park.
Our Mayor, Cllr. Pamela Kearns, officially 
opened the new Tymon Park Centre on 
28 October.  This fantastic new public 
building is designed to provide flexible 
indoor and outdoor space for small and 
medium sized events and activities for the 
local community.  The centre also hosts 
the Park House Café, which is operated 
by local partners Eala (or Swan). This is a 
long-awaited and hugely welcome facility 
for the local area providing a space for 
the community to meet and mingle, with 
indoor and outdoor seating overlooking 
the lake, along with accessibility 
enhancements and facilities for park users 
and an upgrade of the park entrance area 
from Wellington Road with bee-friendly 
planting. 
The new centre is designed to integrate 
with and enhance Tymon Park with a 
community space that grows out of 
the existing stone walls and around an 
existing tree.  The café opens to the park 
with its glazed façade, feature canopy 
and extensive terrace, embracing a south 
facing aspect onto the adjacent lake. The 
project has also delivered an extremely 
attractive landscaped bio-retention area 
by the lake which sustainably manages the 
surface water from the scheme. This small 
pond is surrounded with pollinator friendly 
planting and is cleaning and filtering 
surface water run-off and supporting 
pollinators with colourful plants and 
flowers. The green roof on the building has 
been seeded with meadow seeds, which 
we harvested from local award-winning 
pollinator meadows within the park, and 
will support birds and other wildlife as well 
as managing surface water in a sustainable 
way.
This overall project under our three-year 
capital programme was approximately 
€3m and meets a corporate commitment 
to supporting investment in community 
infrastructure with a focus on enhancing 
local parks.
SDCC’s Parks and Architects teams, 
along with consultant architects, Cotter 
& Naessens Ltd., carried out planning, 
design and project management work on 
this project and the construction work was 
carried out by James Oliver Hearty and 
Sons Ltd.
The Park House Café is now open to the 
public, with Éala serving great coffee and 
a selection of snacks throughout the day.  
The community space within the centre 
will be available for bookings by local 
community groups shortly and can be 
booked online at www.sdcc.ie.
In a further enhancement to Tymon 
Park earlier this month, Mayor Kearns 
officially launched the new “Guardians 
of the Forest” fairy trail in Tymon Park 
alongside local students from Scoil Íosa. 
This new fairy trail has been developed to 
encourage families and children to explore 
the park and connect with nature in a 
creative way. 
The trail features nine fairy houses and 
three carved guardians watching over the 
woodland and was delivered by our public 
realm team at a cost of approximately 
€97,000.
